thread:
alex: heads-up — after the midnight deploy I'm seeing lots of FlashAttention fallbacks on mixtral-16h with 96 head_dim. p50 token latency jumped for some traces.

kim: can you paste a quick profile? which requests are falling back (kv size, seq len, batch size)?

alex: quick numbers from a 1k-sample run: flash p50=10.2ms but fallback rate ~38%. when fallback triggers, sdpa p50=13.1ms, triton p50=20.4ms. fallback appears correlated with batch sizes >8 and seq_len around 256. KV cache hit traces show extra memcpy.

riley: interesting — 96 head_dim is not multiple of 128/64/16 depending on kernels. flash kernels expect head_dim % 8==0 but we have quantization padding differences. any mask error logs?

alex: no explicit mask exception, but we see mismatched mask offsets in logs: "mask_offset != expected" in the kernel selection debug output. dumping one trace: \n```\nKERNEL_SELECT: flash -> fail head_dim_align (96 % 16 != 0)\nFALLBACK_REASON: sdpa_compat\nKV_CACHE: base_ptr=0x7f8a, offset_mismatch=32\n```\n
sam: Deploy-bot: new runtime image rolled to canary (#2024.03.14).

kim: 96 % 16 == 0 actually (96/16=6) — so head_dim aligns to 16. Are we hitting an internal block size that expects 128 multiple because of tile layout? Which backend variant of FlashAttention are we using (flash_attn_v2 vs flash_attn_v1)?

alex: flash_attn_v2. But I suspect our KV packing logic pads per-head to 8 bytes boundary and then a second stage expects 128-block grouping for vectorized loads. Mistral/Mixtral sometimes use odd layout for k/v when using RoPE scaling.

riley: RoPE scale... we introduced dynamic rope_scale per layer for long-context experiments, right? If rope_scale != 1.0 we rewrite positions which changes prefix caching offsets — that could make KV pointers unaligned for fused kernels.

maria: quick test suggestion: try forcing kernel_preference=["sdpa","triton"] for the problematic model to see if latency stabilizes (temporary workaround). Also run small batch sizes to confirm batching heuristic impact.

alex: tried that — forcing sdpa removes fallback churn and reduces p95 jitter, but p50 is slightly higher overall. However it's stable. Forcing triton is too slow.

sam: what's the root cause? if it's pointer alignment we could add KV cache pad logic at allocation time to 256B align. Impact on memory? small for these model sizes.

kim: another angle: our kernel selector checks head_dim and seq_len and global batch. We currently allow cross-model batching if "compatible_layout==true". Maybe compatibility check is too permissive — we should check KV stride and rope_scale equality. If rope_scale differs across requests, fused flash kernels must not be batched together.

alex: exactly. I reproduced a synthetic where two requests batched together — one with rope_scale=1.0, one with 0.75 — flash attempts fused execution and then fails mask alignment at runtime -> fallback for entire batch.

riley: actionable list: 1) tighten batch compatibility: include (rope_scale, kv_stride, per_head_padding) in key; 2) ensure KV allocator can optionally pad per-request base so fused kernels see aligned pointers; 3) add telemetry for fallback reason counts per-model.

maria: +1. Also run a quick profiling sweep across models: Llama-7B, Mistral-7B, Mixtral variants, Qwen-7B with head_dims 64/80/96/128 to map fallback surface. I can schedule that on canary cluster.

alex: attached config I used: \n```\nmodel: mixtral-16h\nhead_dim: 96\nrope_scale: 1.0\nkernel_pref: ["flash","sdpa","triton"]\nbatch_limit: 32\nauto_pad_kv: false\n```\n
kim: thanks. One more important detail: our SDPA fallback currently disables certain fused matmul->softmax kernels which increases memory traffic. If we add a small head_pad to 128 for flash path only, we must also ensure the model serialization records that padding so cache lookups remain consistent across restarts.

alex: noted. For a short-term fix I'm going to: 1) disable cross-rope batching, 2) enable per-request KV alignment pad when head_dim % 32 != 0, 3) drop canary to 50% to verify. Will post numbers in a follow-up.

sam: Deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled at 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC — manual hold until alex confirms.

riley: also add unit test: mixtrals with head_dim in {80,96} and variable rope_scale should exercise kernel selector and assert no fallback when padding enabled.

maria: thanks team — once you have perf numbers post them here. This pattern might explain other recent p95 regressions for long-context chat workloads.

alex: will do. short-term perf numbers after padding change: flash fallback drops from 38% -> 3%, p50 stable (10.4ms -> 10.6ms), p95 improves 40%. I'll open a PR with the alloc pad and selector tightening.

kim: awesome, thanks. If that goes green we should roll to prod and add a changelog note about kernel compatibility and rope_scale constraints. :rocket:
